spec: Build a REST API for personal notes. Users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note has a title, body and timestamps. Notes are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single DynamoDB-backed entity with ordinary CRUD only.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint fetching a single note
Note model has title, body and timestamps

plan.summary: A REST API for managing personal notes. Authenticated-by-header users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes; each note carries a title, body and created/updated timestamps. Notes persist in a single DynamoDB table keyed by user and note id. Deployed as a FastAPI application running in Lambda behind API Gateway, with IAM roles and CloudWatch logging.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe returning service status; used by deployment checks and monitoring.
Create a new note from a JSON body containing title and body; generates note id and created_at/updated_at timestamps.
List the caller's notes with optional pagination (limit, next_token) via a DynamoDB query on the partition key.
Fetch a single note by id; 404 if it does not exist for the caller.
Update the title and/or body of an existing note and refresh updated_at.
Delete a note by id; returns 204 on success, 404 if absent.

data_models.name: Note
fields: user_id: string (partition key, defaults to 'default-user' when no auth header supplied)
note_id: string (sort key, UUID4 generated server-side)

aws_resources.name: notes-table
aws_resources.justification: Spec states notes are stored in DynamoDB; table with partition key user_id and sort key note_id supports all five CRUD operations plus per-user listing.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-function
aws_resources.justification: Hosts the FastAPI application (via an ASGI adapter) so the REST API runs serverlessly without managing servers.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-gateway
aws_resources.justification: Provides the public HTTP entry point and proxies all /notes and /health routes to the Lambda function.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-lambda-role
aws_resources.justification: Execution role for the Lambda granting least-privilege DynamoDB GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Query on the notes table plus CloudWatch Logs write access.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-log-group
aws_resources.justification: Log group for Lambda request/error logs so CRUD failures and latency can be diagnosed.

assumptions: No authentication mechanism was specified; the API reads an optional X-User-Id header to scope notes per user and falls back to 'default-user', keeping the data model multi-tenant-ready without adding Cognito (unavailable in LocalStack Community).
'Personal notes' implies per-user isolation, so user_id is the DynamoDB partition key and every read/write is scoped to the caller's id.
Timestamps are server-generated ISO-8601 UTC strings; clients cannot set them.
DynamoDB billing mode is PAY_PER_REQUEST since no throughput requirements were given.
Listing returns newest-first is not required by the spec; results are returned in DynamoDB sort-key order with a default page size of 25 and a max of 100.
PUT is treated as a partial update (only supplied fields change) because the spec says 'update' without describing full replacement semantics.
No file attachments, search, sharing, notifications or async processing were requested, so S3, SQS, SNS and Secrets Manager are intentionally omitted.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → personal_notes_api (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:notes-table, Lambda:notes-api-function, API Gateway:notes-api-gateway, IAM:notes-api-lambda-role, CloudWatch:notes-api-log-group

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 6 files — FastAPI notes API with a decoupled storage layer. `storage.py` defines a `NotesRepository` interface, a DynamoDB implementation (boto3 resource honouring `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` and defaulting to us-east-1/`notes-table`, conditional writes mapped to `NoteNotFoundError`, opaque base64 pagination tokens) and an in-memory implementation. `app.py` wires the six planned endpoints (`/health`, CRUD on `/notes`) with pydantic models, per-user scoping via the optional `X-User-Id` header (fallback `default-user`), server-generated ISO-8601 timestamps, partial PUT semantics, 204 delete, and uniform `{detail, code}` error bodies. Tests use `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` with dependency-overridden in-memory repo plus a fake boto3 table/resource for the DynamoDB path — fully offline, no network. requirements.txt lists only fastapi, uvicorn, boto3, pydantic; README documents config and run/test commands.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for personal_notes_api mapping 1:1 to the plan's aws_resources.

Files: versions.tf (terraform block, hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 plus archive/local for inline Lambda packaging), variables.tf (defaults notes-table, notes-api-function, notes-api-gateway, notes-api-lambda-role, /aws/lambda/notes-api-function), main.tf, outputs.tf.

Resources:
- DynamoDB notes-table: PAY_PER_REQUEST, hash key user_id, range key note_id, SSE with a customer managed KMS CMK, point-in-time recovery enabled.
- Lambda notes-api-function: Python handler written by local_file and zipped by the archive_file data source (no pre-built artifact needed). It implements /health and full CRUD on /notes via boto3 against the table, honouring X-User-Id with a default-user fallback, 25/100 page sizes, base64 next_token pagination, partial PUT updates and 404/422 error bodies ({detail, code}). Hardened with reserved concurrency, CMK-encrypted env vars and active tracing.
- API Gateway notes-api-gateway: REGIONAL REST API with root ANY and {proxy+} ANY AWS_PROXY integrations, lambda invoke permission, deployment with redeployment trigger and create_before_destroy, stage with X-Ray tracing plus JSON access logging, and method settings with INFO logging/metrics.
- IAM notes-api-lambda-role: assume-role for lambda.amazonaws.com and one least-privilege policy — DynamoDB GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Query on the table ARN (+/index/*), kms use on the single CMK, logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on the function log group only. No wildcard actions or resources.
- CloudWatch: Lambda log group (plan's notes-api-log-group) and an API Gateway access log group, both 365-day retention and CMK encrypted.
- KMS CMK with rotation and a scoped key policy is included solely to satisfy the encryption-at-rest checks for DynamoDB, Lambda env vars and log groups (KMS is available in LocalStack Community).

Provider has default_tags with project and managed-by. Checks that are impossible under LocalStack Community or contradict the spec (Lambda VPC/DLQ/code signing, API auth, WAF, mTLS, API caching) carry inline checkov:skip comments with justifications; no RDS/ECS/EKS/ElastiCache is used.
